div.head: Attachment
div.p: AN APPROACH TO THE ARAB REFUGEE PROBLEM

list.label: a.
list.item: Ascertain in Ankara availability of Ambassador Kural or other qualified Turk emissary.
list.label: b.
list.item: Hold secret session of PCC providing emissary with whatever credentials and instructions are needed.
list.label: c.
list.item: Emissary to visit Tel Aviv to discuss on most secret basis with Ben Gurion and Mrs. Meir optional repatriation plan, emphasizing PCC assurances that no mass influx of refugees or serious security threat need be feared.
list.label: d.
list.item: Visit Arab host country capitals to discuss with leaders on most secret basis proposed optional repatriation plan, emphasizing that principle of repatriation will be upheld but that realistically implementation would have to be on a phased and optional basis.
list.label: e.
list.item: In both Israel and Arab capitals recall UNGA resolution of last November and note that PCC will be required to report what it has done. Such report would, of course, include a discussion of the attitudes of the governments directly concerned.

list.label: a.
list.item: PCC to invite Arabs and Israel to send representatives to a meeting to consider the refugee problem.
list.label: b.
list.item: Outline to the conferees basic elements of the problem, including particularly pertinent UN directives. Obtain conferees views.
list.label: c.
list.item:
Set forth PCC thesis that refugees should be allowed to choose: 1)
repatriation as law-abiding citizens of Israel, 2)
settlement in an Arab country, or 3)
settlement in a non-Arab country.
Restitution or compensation will be considered in each case as appropriate.
list.label: d.
list.item: Announce that PCC intends to conduct a refugee referendum. Describe how it works and accept suggestions for improvement.

list.label: a.
list.item: Invite refugees to come to PCC-sponsored rehabilitation stations.
list.label: b.
list.item: In private let refugees express their preferences re 2c above.
list.label: c.
list.item: At same time, obtain important information concerning each refugee, both as to his pre-1948 and his post-1948 status.
list.label: d.
list.item: Let the impression be given that without this voluntary application at rehabilitation stations refugees can expect no claim in the future as to repatriation or compensation.

list.label: a.
list.item: Review PCC initiatives since the preceding UNGA.
list.label: b.
list.item: Obtain UNGA support for approach being taken by PCC.
list.label: c.
list.item: Urge member governments to open their doors to refugees who might wish to settle in non-Arab countries.
list.label: d.
list.item: Incorporate above in a resolution.

list.label: a.
list.item: Establish priorities for those wishing to become law-abiding citizens of Israel.
list.label: b.
list.item: Arrange with Israel Government the machinery for permitting refugees at a rate of about 24,000 per year to return to Israel and become useful citizens.
list.label: c.
list.item: Arrange appropriate PCC supervision to assure refugees obtain a fair break.

list.label: a.
list.item: Arrange with Arab host countries and subsidize projects for making refugees productive citizens in the Arab countries.
list.label: b.
list.item: Make appropriate arrangements with non-Arab countries willing to take refugees.

list.label: a.
list.item: Assist Jordan in taking care of those refugees who have neither submitted to repatriation or resettlement.

note.p: Confidential. Drafted by Meyer on May 24.
